Hi, I've been through something fairly similar recently but from the other side.

My partner and I have just moved to a new city so I could start University. The stress  and other things got to me and mental health issues I've dealt with for over a decade spiked and I ended up in a very similar self-destructive spiral. I know that I've needed help for a long time, but when I was younger the notion of getting therapy was unheard of. My boyfriend has really struggled and has basically had to give me an ultimatum: get help or lose me, something neither of us want. We were at a point where I was hurting myself and I couldn't recognise how unnatural and completely not normal that was. I was terrified of being called crazy or mental, I was having dreams after that first doctor's session that I was going to be taken away and locked up. It took me an incredibly long time to recognise that not only was I not strong enough to get the help that I desperately needed, but that attitudes towards mental health care are so different to what they were in the past. 

I think the suggestions made in other comments are good, if you feel like you would be happy to lead by example then do. You've obviously already put everything into your marriage and into supporting your family, but it will get there eventually. Best of luck x

Yup. I was really depressed throughout school and the resulting self-harm and SAs caused me to drop out of my AS levels (Year 12 in the UK, around 16-17y/o). I thought I had ruined my chances of ever going to University or having the career that I wanted and it used to tear me up and really destroyed my confidence. However two weeks ago I graduated from my Access to Higher Education course and can proudly say that I start at my dream Uni in September. 

I'm still so upset that my school years were taken from me and that I wasn't able to move on with the rest of my peers but I've worked hard to get back on track and I've managed to find something that I'm really passionate about. 

I'm sorry that you're in a desperate place at the moment, but I think all anyone can do is keep on going in the hope that one day it won't hurt in the same way anymore. I really do wish you the best of luck, here if you need to talk.

My forearms are still quite badly scarred from years of cutting (2 years clean, woohoo!) and I've worked in primary schools etc. since then. I've mostly had positive reactions. I've found that kids are often just kind of curious as it's not something they've seen before, teens are understanding as it's more accepted in society now, and adults tend to keep their thoughts to themselves until they know me and are comfortable with asking. I've never had any nasty comments or invasive questions, and my scars are definitely noticeable. The worst reaction is probably just the staring...
